gloss: law · method · model — and, in Buddhist texts, dharma
glossUnihan: law, rule, regulation, statute; France, French
form: 氵 (water) + 去 (remove); the older 灋 adds 廌
formNote: The Shuowen gives the full form 灋 and explains it: 刑也。平之如水，从水；廌，所以觸不直者去之，从去 — “punishment; level as water, hence water; 廌, the beast that butts the crooked and removes them, hence 去.” The account is the Han dictionary’s; whether it reflects the graph’s origin is debated.
summary: A standard to follow: law, method, model, and as a verb, “to take as a model”. Buddhist translators made 法 their word for dharma in both its senses: the teaching, and the basic elements of experience.
placement: On the right of the sphere, below its equator, mirroring 有 across the hollow axis. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: The Teaching, and the Elements
satellites.evidence: 法 renders dharma throughout Chinese Buddhism: the Buddha’s teaching (佛法), and in Abhidharma the basic elements of experience, divided into the conditioned (有為法) and the unconditioned (無為法). The older Chinese sense, “standard, model”, made it a natural fit.
satellites.caveat: The conditioned / unconditioned division also appears on 為’s card (無為 · asaṃskṛta), read from 為’s side.

satellites.title: The Beast That Removes the Crooked
satellites.evidence: The Shuowen’s 灋 combines water (氵), “level as water”, with 廌, a one-horned beast said to butt the guilty party in a dispute, and 去, “to remove”. Law is pictured as levelling and removing what is crooked.
satellites.caveat: A moralised Han explanation. It is not settled as the graph’s origin, and the legend of the beast (獬豸) is a legend.
